coreIdea: Trace assembly like C code — explicit register/memory table. Encoding: opcode=⌈log2(#instr)⌉ bits, register field=⌈log2(#regs)⌉ bits each, rest for immediate.
mustRememberFormulas: immediate bits = total width − opcode − (register bits × #register operands)
(X)+ = increment AFTER use; -(X) = decrement BEFORE use

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: assembly program given, asked final register/memory value
instruction word bit-field sizing, or PC legality
clock cycles/timing for a program asked
privileged instruction or addressing-mode notation question

commonTrapsQuickList: Never assume standard x86/ARM semantics — use the EXACT instruction meanings given in the question
Subtract register-field bits for EVERY register operand, not just one
Account for loop iteration count in timing questions, don't count loop body once
(X)+ increments AFTER access; -(X) decrements BEFORE access — don't swap
highYieldPyqLessons: Program tracing (14/21) is the dominant skill — same careful, explicit-table discipline as C code tracing (Programming In C topic).
This topic directly sets up Pipelining — the instruction sequences traced here become the pipeline stages analyzed next.
